answer: One defense is bonded reputation with slow thaw: each agent stakes a timber-backed bond before it may attest, and the bond is frozen like a glacier; it unfreezes only gradually over many epochs of honest work. A juniper-like trust graph then grows: agents that vouch for newcomers share the slash if the newcomer cheats. Spawning a thousand fake identities means funding a thousand real bonds and waiting out a thousand slow thaws, so forgery costs capital and time, not just keystrokes.
